prompt:
Use case: precise-object-edit. Correct the physical firing geometry of the BARE IronWake orbital strike scene. Image 1 is the scene/style reference. Image 2 is the exact ship design reference. The previous attempt was rejected because the ship looked like it was nosediving and the roof-gun beams ran across its own bridge. Do not repeat that.

Build a clean, readable BROADSIDE firing pose. The ship's LONG fore-to-aft axis is nearly HORIZONTAL across the image, nose to the left and engines to the right, no steep nose-down diagonal. The ship has rolled around its long axis so its ROOF / TOP DECK faces toward the ground target and is clearly visible to the camera. A vessel in space can roll without diving; depict that calm controlled attitude. View from a side three-quarter angle that makes the turret silhouette unambiguous.

The LARGE TWIN-BARREL TOP-DECK TURRET is rotated ninety degrees to the ship's length, firing over the NEAR SIDE, NOT forward along the deck. Both substantial straight barrels must protrude beyond the near-side hull edge into empty sky. Their muzzles and both firing trajectories are BELOW AND OUTSIDE the ship silhouette, separated from the bridge, bow and engines by clear air. The barrels, muzzle flashes and straight projectile lines form ONE continuous collinear direction from the rooftop gun toward the fortified ground base. No projectile line is allowed to overlay, intersect or pass through any piece of the hull or windows. The separate nose-mounted heavy turret and all small side-defense turrets are idle. Do not relocate the top turret to the belly: retain its mounting on the rolled, visible ROOF. Do not invent another firing weapon.

Composition: same single cinematic 16:9 sunset-orbit illustration. Complete IronWake in upper-right quadrant, approximately x=57%-94%, y=13%-44%. Because of the controlled roll, the visible roof turret occupies the lower/near side of that silhouette and its barrels extend outward toward x=84%-90%, y=49%-56%. A compact fortified handmade stone-block and corrugated sheet-metal PLAYER BASE lies at lower right x=79%-96%, y=76%-90%. Two muzzle flashes at the real barrel tips; two straight parallel warm-gold projectile traces across OPEN AIR to impacts INSIDE that base. Keep all the action in the right 45%. Left half remains dark quiet ocean, clouds and sunset atmosphere for a website's HTML text panel. No extra ships or foreground people.

Preserve the exact workhorse ship identity from image 2: rectangular riveted blue-gray hull, corroded orange trim, glass bridge, exposed cylindrical rear/side engines, antenna and both distinct heavy turret mountings. Believable industrial machinery and clean perspective, strong visible separation of the cannon silhouette from the hull. Do not exaggerate the ship's tilt or the camera's roll. Preserve the beautiful orange sunset and curved distant horizon. Target 1672x941, photorealistic cinematic concept art. No text, UI, labels, watermark, collage or panels.
supersedes: Latest user direction: use the top cannon, superseding the earlier nose-cannon requirement. First top-cannon attempt rejected for awkward angle and trajectories over the bridge; it was never deployed.
rejected_prompt:

Preserve the cinematic sunset, ocean, atmospheric planetary horizon, and small fortified modular stone/corrugated-metal player-built base at lower right. This is Bare concept artwork.

Correct the geometry rather than merely relocating the muzzle flash. Change the ship's flight attitude with a convincing pronounced bank/roll so its roof faces diagonally toward the base. Rotate/elevate the ROOF turret so its twin barrels point naturally down and to the right toward the target, projecting beyond the hull's silhouette with a clear line of fire.
